title_en: Bai Xiang Food Co., Ltd. v. Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office and Chen Zhaohui (Third Party) — administrative dispute over invalidation of a design patent

full_text_en:
[Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. v. Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office and Third Party Chen Zhaohui — administrative dispute over invalidation of design patent right]

[Ruling Summary]

In the trial of administrative dispute cases concerning the grant and confirmation of design patent rights, when applying Article 23(3) of the Patent Law to determine whether the exclusive right to use a registered trademark constitutes a lawful prior right, as long as the trademark application date is before the patent application date, and the trademark has been approved for registration and remains valid at the time the request for invalidation of the patent is filed, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark from the prior application can oppose the design patent right from the later application, and be used to determine whether the design patent right conflicts with it.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Ruling

(2014) Zhi Xing Zi No. 4

Re-review Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office. Domicile: Yingu Building, No. 9, North Fourth Ring West Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Maoyu, Deputy Director of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jiali, Examiner of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wan Qi, Examiner of the Board.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. (formerly Henan Zhenglong Food Co., Ltd.). Domicile: Gongmao Development Zone, Xuedian Town, Xinzheng City, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Yao Zhongliang, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wen Biaofei, male, Han ethnicity, patent agent of Taiyuan Kewei Patent Agency, residing in Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Yongjie, employee of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Chen Zhaohui, male, Han ethnicity, Chairman of Sichuan Baijia Food Co., Ltd., residing in Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Re-review Applicant Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board), in the case of the administrative dispute over invalidation of design patent right with Respondent Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. (formerly Henan Zhenglong Food Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Baixiang Company) and Third Party at First Instance Chen Zhaohui, dissatisfied with the administrative judgment of the Beijing High People's Court (2011) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 1733, applied to this Court for re-review. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

The Patent Reexamination Board applied for re-review, asserting: (1) The second instance judgment's finding that the prior right asserted by Baixiang Company was the trademark application right based on the prior trademark application violated the principle of request. Under the principle of request, the Patent Reexamination Board generally only examines the request, reasons, and evidence presented by the party requesting invalidation, and does not bear the obligation of comprehensive review of patent validity. In this case, Baixiang Company never raised the ground of invalidation that this patent conflicted with its prior trademark application right during the invalidation procedure, but instead raised the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as the prior right. It was only in its second instance defense that Baixiang Company asserted the trademark application right. The second instance judgment, by reason that the appealed decision did not examine whether this patent conflicted with the trademark application right, set aside the appealed decision, which lacked factual and legal basis. (2) The second instance judgment's conclusion that the trademark application right constituted a prior right under Article 23 of the Patent Law of the PRC as amended in 2000 (hereinafter referred to as the 2000 Patent Law) was an error in the application of law. A prior right must be a lawful right with a legal basis; otherwise, the implementation of a patent could not constitute infringement, and no conflict of rights would arise. Under the Trademark Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law), there is no such thing as a trademark application right. Nor does the trademark application right fall within the "rights related to trademark review" as provided in the Trademark Review Rules. (3) Even if the trademark application right were considered a lawful right, a design patent right would not conflict with it. The conflict of rights referred to in Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law means that a design patent uses the subject matter of a prior lawful right without the permission of the prior right holder, such that the implementation of the patent will harm the relevant lawful rights or interests of the prior right holder. Whether the trademark application right is understood as a right to claim or a property right, its core remains the qualification to obtain the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. Under the Trademark Law, the implementation of a design patent does not prevent the exercise of the trademark application right, including the applicant's disposition of the trademark application, nor does it harm the trademark applicant's later acquisition of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as a matter of right. In other words, the trademark applicant's interest in obtaining the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is not harmed, and the elements of infringement are not satisfied. In fact, the implementation of a design patent may cause consumers to mistakenly believe that goods using the design originate from another manufacturer, which actually infringes the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, not the trademark application right. The trademark application right cannot be the object of infringement by the implementation of a design patent. In summary, the first and second instance judgments were unclear in fact finding and erroneous in the application of law. It requested that the first and second instance judgments be set aside and that Decision No. 14261 on the Request for Invalidation (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 14261) be upheld.

Baixiang Company submitted its opinion, stating: The re-review application of the Patent Reexamination Board lacks factual and legal basis. It requested that the application be dismissed.

This Court, upon review, finds: In respect of this request for invalidation, the oral hearing record of the Patent Reexamination Board dated November 18, 2009, states on page 4: "Presiding Examiner: Requesting party, as to the prior acquisition, what time point is used? Requesting party: The trademark right was applied for on December 12, 1997. The trademark application date is used as the time of prior acquisition, which is before the application date of this patent, and therefore it conflicts with the lawful right acquired by another person in advance."

The trademark No. 1506193 held by Baixiang Company had an application date of December 12, 1997, a preliminary approval announcement date of October 14, 2000, and an approval and registration date of January 14, 2001. The design patent No. 00333252.7 for a product named "Food Packaging Bag" (i.e., this patent) was filed by Chen Zhaohui on October 16, 2000, and was announced for grant on May 2, 2001.

Henan Zhenglong Food Co., Ltd. changed its name to Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. upon approval on June 28, 2012.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute in this case are: whether the second instance judgment's finding that the prior right asserted by Baixiang Company was the trademark application right violated the principle of request; and whether this patent would conflict with the prior trademark application right.

(I) Whether the second instance judgment's finding that the prior right asserted by Baixiang Company was the trademark application right violated the principle of request

First, according to Decision No. 14261, when Baixiang Company filed the request for invalidation, its ground was that this patent did not comply with Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law. In its supplementary opinion statement, it also stated that "an important part of the design of this patent conflicts with the lawful right acquired by the requesting party in advance, and should be declared invalid." It can be seen that Baixiang Company raised the ground of invalidation that this patent conflicted with a lawful right acquired in advance during the invalidation proceedings. Second, according to the oral hearing record in the invalidation proceedings, Baixiang Company clearly stated during the oral hearing that it used the trademark application date as the time of prior acquisition of the lawful right, and that this time was before the application date of this patent, so this patent conflicted with the lawful right it acquired in advance. Baixiang Company had already clearly designated the time point of prior acquisition of its lawful right as the trademark application date. The Patent Reexamination Board and the first instance court both considered that the prior right referred to in Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law should be the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, and did not support Baixiang Company's assertion. Therefore, Baixiang Company further clearly raised the concept of the trademark application right in its second instance defense. Considering the above facts comprehensively, the second instance court's determination that the prior right asserted by Baixiang Company was the trademark application right based on the prior trademark application did not violate the principle of request.

(II) Whether this patent would conflict with the prior trademark application right

Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law provides: "A design for which a patent is granted shall not be identical or similar to any design which, before the date of filing, has been publicly disclosed in publications anywhere in the world or has been publicly used in China, and shall not conflict with any lawful right acquired by another person in advance." After a design patent is granted following a formal examination, its implementation may conflict with rights lawfully acquired by another person before the application date, harming the lawful rights of the prior right holder. To resolve conflicts of rights, it is first necessary to clarify the specific content of the prior lawful right. Article 16 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases provides: "The lawful rights acquired in advance referred to in Article 23 of the Patent Law include: trademark rights, copyright, enterprise name rights, portrait rights, rights to use a distinctive packaging or get-up of a well-known commodity, etc." According to this provision, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is one of the lawful rights acquired in advance referred to in Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law. If a design for the same kind of goods or similar goods adopts an identifier identical or similar to another person's registered trademark, the implementation of the design patent may cause relevant members of the public to mistakenly believe that the goods originate from the trademark owner, thereby harming the trademark owner's lawful rights and causing a conflict between the design patent right and the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. The criterion for determining such a conflict is essentially whether the implementation of the design patent would infringe the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. In this case, the approval and registration date of trademark No. 1506193 was after the application date of this patent. The exclusive right to use a registered trademark was not acquired in advance; only the trademark application date preceded the application date of this patent. The prior right asserted by Baixiang Company was also the trademark application right based on the prior trademark application. In this regard, this Court holds that where the trademark application date precedes the design patent application date, a design patent right will not conflict with a trademark application right, and the trademark application right cannot serve as a lawful right acquired in advance under Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law. However, based on the nature and function of the trademark application right itself and the principle of protecting prior rights, as long as the trademark application date is before the patent application date, and at the time the request for invalidation of the patent is filed, the trademark has been approved for registration and remains valid, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark from the prior application can oppose the design patent right from the later application, and be used to determine whether the design patent right conflicts with it. The reasons are as follows:

1. The legal nature of the trademark application right. First, under the principle of first-to-file in the Trademark Law, where two or more applicants apply to register identical or similar trademarks for the same kind of goods or similar goods, the Trademark Office accepts the earliest filed trademark registration application. In other words, once an applicant files a trademark registration application, from the application date, they enjoy the right to exclude others from applying to register identical or similar trademarks for the same kind of goods or similar goods. Second, under the relevant provisions of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Trademark Law of the PRC, an applicant may assign their trademark registration application, meaning the applicant can dispose of the trademark application right as a civil right or interest according to their own will. Finally, the ultimate goal of a trademark application, that is, the realization of the trademark application right, is the registration of the trademark. From this perspective, the trademark application right is an expectation right, a kind of expectation of obtaining the exclusive right to use a registered trademark in the future. It exists from the date of trademark application and is finally realized upon the approval and registration of the trademark. In summary, the trademark application right itself is a realistic and lawful right or interest, and in nature, it is an expectation right to the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, and should be protected by law.

2. The role of the trademark application right in determining conflicts of rights. The trademark application right is a lawful right or interest. Where the trademark application date precedes the design patent application date, the implementation of the design patent will not affect whether the trademark is ultimately approved for registration, and there will be no issue of conflict between the design patent right and the trademark application right. Therefore, the trademark application right cannot serve as a lawful right acquired in advance under Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law. The second instance court held that the lawful right acquired in advance asserted by Baixiang Company was the trademark application right, and that Decision No. 14261 should determine whether this patent conflicted with the trademark application right. This was an error in the application of law, and this Court hereby corrects it. The trademark application right cannot be used as a prior right under Article 23 of the 2000 Patent Law to determine whether a design patent right conflicts with it. However, the trademark application right is of great significance for determining conflicts between design patent rights and the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, as reflected in the following: As an expectation right, the complete right ultimately expected from the trademark application right is the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. Only when the trademark is registered is the ultimate interest of the trademark application realized. At that point, the trademark application right should be protected retroactively, confirming the legal significance of the trademark application date for the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. As long as the trademark application date is before the design patent application date, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark from the prior application can oppose the design patent right from the later application.

3. The principle of protecting prior rights. In this case, after trademark No. 1506193 was registered, the implementation of this patent might objectively conflict with that trademark. However, the trademark was filed in advance. Compared to the trademark, this patent is not a prior right. The resolution of such a conflict can only follow the principle of protecting prior rights, holding that the exclusive right to use a registered trademark from Baixiang Company's prior application can be used to oppose Chen Zhaohui's design patent right. Moreover, the preliminary approval announcement date of trademark No. 1506193 was also before the application date of this patent. For a trademark that has been preliminarily examined and announced, the Trademark Office has conducted a preliminary examination of the trademark application and found it to be in compliance with the Trademark Law. The purpose of the announcement is to solicit opinions from relevant operators and the public. During the announcement period, interested persons may file an opposition with the Trademark Office. The application date of this patent was after the preliminary approval announcement date of trademark No. 1506193. Objectively, there was a possibility that the design patent applicant imitated or copied the prior filed trademark. This situation is also the main object of prevention by the legislation of Article 23 of the Patent Law.

In this case, the application date of Baixiang Company's trademark No. 1506193 was before the application date of this patent. After trademark No. 1506193 was approved for registration, it remained valid at the time Baixiang Company filed this request for invalidation of the patent. The exclusive right to use the registered trademark No. 1506193 can oppose this patent and be used to determine whether this patent conflicts with it. The Patent Reexamination Board, solely because the approval and registration date of trademark No. 1506193 was after the application date of this patent, held that the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1506193 could not be used to determine whether this patent conflicted with it. This was an error in the application of law. The second instance court's judgment that the Patent Reexamination Board should make a new invalidation decision had a correct conclusion. As to whether this patent would conflict with the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1506193, this should be specifically determined by the Patent Reexamination Board in its new invalidation decision.

In summary, the re-review application of the Patent Reexamination Board does not satisfy the conditions set forth in Article 63, Paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 72 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. Pursuant to Article 74 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

The re-review application of the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Zhou Xiang
Acting Judge: Luo Xia
Acting Judge: Zhou Yunchuan

October 11, 2014

Clerk: Zhang Bo

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]
Senior Judge Zhou Xiang, born in 1972, Doctor of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2011.
